title: Polynomial Function
intro: A polynomial is a sum of terms aₙxⁿ + … + a₁x + a₀. Degree = highest power. Leading coefficient decides end behaviour.

cards.title: Representation of Quadratic Functions
body: **Representation of Quadratic Functions.** A polynomial is built from terms aₙxⁿ. Degree is the highest power with a ≠ 0.
For a **quadratic** ax² + bx + c (a ≠ 0): the graph is a parabola. a > 0 opens up; a < 0 opens down.
Remember the three forms: **standard** ax²+bx+c, **vertex** a(x−h)²+k, **factored** a(x−r₁)(x−r₂). Switch forms to read intercepts, vertex, and roots quickly.

cards.title: Three forms of a quadratic function
body: A **quadratic function** has the form f(x) = ax² + bx + c with a ≠ 0. Its graph is a **parabola**: it opens upward if a > 0 and downward if a < 0.
**Standard form:** f(x) = ax² + bx + c (the y-intercept is c). **Vertex form:** f(x) = a(x − h)² + k (vertex (h, k), axis of symmetry x = h). **Factored form:** f(x) = a(x − r₁)(x

cards.title: Polynomial basics
body: A polynomial is aₙxⁿ+…+a₁x+a₀. Degree = highest power with a≠0.
Leading coefficient aₙ sets end behaviour: for even degree, both ends same side; odd degree, opposite sides.

cards.title: Factor & remainder tips
body: Factor theorem: (x−a) divides f iff f(a)=0.
Synthetic division speeds polynomial division by (x−a).
Graph crosses x-axis at real roots; multiplicity even → touch & turn.

cards.title: Worked example: vertex and axis
cards.problem: Find the vertex of f(x) = x² − 4x + 1 and write it in vertex form.

steps.text: f(2) = 4 − 8 + 1 = −3, so the vertex is **(2, −3)**; axis x = 2.

cards.answer: Vertex form: f(x) = (x − 2)² − 3. Since a = 1 > 0 the minimum value is −3.
